sources.quote: Today, 469 pieces of geography still contain the replacement word in their name, according to the geographic names database managed by the U.S. Geological Survey.
sources.searcher_note: Same measure, same GNIS database: 469 federal names still carry 'negro' (the 1962 Udall replacement word) as of early 2022. The lead has 438 after dropping 50 Spanish 'negro' names by hand. No squaw comparison.

sources.quote: At least 558 place names across the nation include derogatory words referring to African Americans, Vocativ's data analysis found.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found. A 2015 data analysis of federal place names: 558 anti-Black names, most containing 'negro'; 828 'squaw' names. Broader measure than the lead's (it includes other anti-Black terms).

sources.quote: The BGN voted on the final replacement names for 650 names in September 2022 and for 7 additional names in January 2023.
sources.searcher_note: Government count of the squaw renaming: 657 names, Sept 2022 + Jan 2023. The lead says 641 changed in 2020-23. Gives no count of remaining 'Negro' names.

sources.quote: The Department of the Interior today announced the Board on Geographic Names (BGN) has voted on the final replacement names for nearly 650 geographic features featuring the word sq___.
sources.searcher_note: Primary record of the bulk squaw renaming (the comparison half of the lead). Doesn't mention 'Negro' names.

sources.quote: On September 18, 2024 the U.S. Board on Geographic Names approved proposals to change the name of Negro Jack Creek in Tillamook County to Jack Creek
sources.searcher_note: Shows one-at-a-time 'Negro' renamings continued after the lead's 2023-03-17 citation cutoff (two Oregon features, Sept 2024). Supports the lead's caveat; not a count. Nonprofit history group.

notes: The 'Negro' names still on federal maps are covered, with counts: Vocativ 2015 (558 anti-Black names overall), Atmos 2022 (469 with 'negro'). The squaw renaming is fully covered by government sources: about 650 in Sept 2022 plus 7 in Jan 2023. No source found puts the two side by side as the lead does (641 squaw vs at least 41 Negro/n-word renamings in 2020-23), and none has 438, 426, the 105 n-word former names or the 41. The Atmos 469 is about 7% above the lead's 438; the lead removed 50 Spanish 'negro' (black) names that raw counts include. Other counts seen, not recorded: NBC News 2012 said 621 places (page wouldn't render); Axios 2021 was cited in a snippet for 469 (HTTP 403). The Washington Post, 2021-12-17, 'Offensive place names dot the American landscape. Efforts to change them are about to get a lot faster.', was 403 and timed out; not recorded. Eos (2021) repeats Vocativ's 558. No July-Sept 2026 coverage found.
